items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: and then my oldest sister, whose name was Marian, was the third.

ctx.x: As I said, in the beginning, my really feelings about any kind of music, it always seems to be through the eyes of the piano. I remember one time reading where...I think it was Andres Segovia made a statement that at some period in his life, he married his guitar. So I don't know... I never quite went through the ceremony of marrying the piano. But I think we struck up kind of a love at first sight thing, just as I said before, where I was always fascinated by the keyboard.

Back in Red Springs, North Carolina, as I first remember, we lived in my grandmother's house, which we always called The Big House. Later on, my brothers and my father and his brothers, my uncles, they built a small little house themselves out about a half-a-mile away from my grandmother's house. I guess you would call it a log cabin of some sort, because they split the rails and built it themselves. My parents stayed there until after my sister was born, which was the third child.
